newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian leu retail rate sinks before elections.
newsitem.headline: Romanian leu retail rate sinks before elections.

text.p: Romania's leu currency slipped on the retail currency market over the weekend in a fit of nerves two weeks before a general election, prompted by a prediction of a steep plunge.
It slid to 4,000-4,500 to the dollar at the weekend from 3,600 on Friday before clawing its way back on Monday to 3,800-4,000.
The leu remained at 3,305/10 on the interbank market, where economists say the government is propping the currency up ahead of the election.
"There was panic over the weekend and the downswing emerged much earlier than anyone thought," said a Bucharest retail trader. "Tensions have yet to cool down."
The fall amounted to a delayed reaction to a statement by a senior banker last week that the leu was considerably overvalued and had a true value closer to 5,500 to 6,000 to the dollar.
Rates on both the inter-bank market and at retail outlets had held generally steady for three days after the forecast.
The central bank (BNR) said the dip was an emotional reaction to events on the black market and predicted that the currency would rebound.
"Some exchange houses followed the fall on the black market but there are no objective factors to keep the leu so weak," said BNR communication manager Adrian Vasilescu.
Traders have taken a wait-and-see attitude but most of them labelled the forecast plunge as too pessimistic.

"We were expecting the leu to hit fresh lows against the dollar after the elections," said a trader with a broker bank. "It might start this downward trend sooner but I don't think we will witness a sharp move."
But traders said pressure was building on the leu amid traditional winter hoarding of dollars and rising orders for oil and other cold-weather imports.
The leu -- and charges that the government is bolstering it -- have become issues in the final stages of the November 3 presidential and parliamentary elections.
Incumbent Ion Iliescu leads polls for the presidential race but his ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) has been pushed into second and even third place in the parliamentary vote.
The leu has fallen gradually at banks from 2,600 at the beginning of the year. At exchange points, the currency started the year at about 3,000.
"As energy prices are adjusted upward to take account of moves downward by the leu, the currency becomes Romania's Achilles' heel," said one banker.

As offers of dollars are scarce at the government-backed rate on the interbank market, importers wishing to complete deals have resorted to using cross-rates, especially the less traded Belgian franc or Swedish crown. These yield a leu-dollar rate of about 3,700, against 3,550 last week.
Central bank governor Mugur Isarescu recently said the leu-dollar rate should ease to 3,400/3,500.
